mark: Its SP gather bench at T>=6144: gain beyond the interval, bit-exact
mark_reading: The PR's T>=6144 gain is SPRows.project_exchange_rows (ENGRAM_SLICE_TOKENS 2048 -> 6144 and the sliced copy_self=False side-stream pipeline); SPRows.gather_mxfp8 falls back to grouped PyNCCL above the one-shot cap (ring4 from T=2048, direct from T=4096) in both arms. So at T>=6144 the mark is judged on project_exchange_rows; gather_mxfp8 is reported at every T.
hosts: sp1..sp4 (spark-0009..spark-0012), NVIDIA GB10, one rank per node, 200G dual-rail switched RoCE (rocep1s0f0, roceP2p1s0f0); tp4-switched profile of releases/spark-ds41f-1107/cluster.json
image: spark-ds41f:1107 sha256:3f32a962ce04b7c8d85337cd427a8946b8b6bcaadd97cc8d8a8cd14e8d68a6ce on all four nodes (no build)

arms.candidate-49: 1107 image with 0762..0767 applied to the image's vLLM tree (7 vLLM files bound read-only); sp_prefill.py sha256 58e7f2579b73...
arms.baseline: candidate-49 without #979: 1107 image with 0762..0765 and 0767; differs from candidate-49 in sp_prefill.py only (sha256 880ff323bde3...), so it isolates #979

bench: scripts/bench_979_integrated.py: the workload of the PR's bench_sp_focused.py (pr-bench-scripts/, found on sp2..sp4 /tmp; the PR itself ships only receipts) - same T, shapes, seeds, project (Engram wkv [6400, 6144] BF16 matmul) and then (RankOrderParts([4, L, 5120]).sum()), MXFP8 gather tensors with top-k 6, topology settings, 12 warmup and 40 timed iterations with a barrier before each. It times each tree's own SPRows.project_exchange_rows(slices=engram_slices(T), then=...) as engram.py calls it and SPRows.gather_mxfp8 as kernels.py calls it, instead of the PR script's in-script reimplementations (which would be identical code in both arms). Added: T=8192, a seeded engram weight, per-rank timings (max-rank and rank0), output digests, and in-process anchors that are the same code in both arms.
method: Same session (11:44-11:53Z), ABBA per topology: candidate-49 boot1, baseline boot1, baseline boot2, candidate-49 boot2; ring4 then direct. Each boot is a fresh 4-container launch; each rank did ~240 ms of back-to-back 4096^3 BF16 GEMMs before anything was timed. Metric: median over 40 iterations of the per-iteration max over the 4 ranks of CUDA-event time; rank0's median alongside (the PR's script reports rank 0). Interval: the two boots' medians of an arm; 'gain' or 'loss' when the arms' intervals do not overlap. Each boot also has a bootstrap 95% CI of its median.

measured.pr_claim_T6144: -9.0% to -21.6% (853-2,226 us) across the PR's boots and both topologies

bit_exact_detail: At every T, op and topology, each rank's output digest (sha256 of the real rows of project_exchange_rows; of values, scales, weights and ids for gather_mxfp8) is equal across all four runs (two candidate-49, two baseline), and every rank's output equals its in-process anchor (serial project + exchange_rows; grouped PyNCCL all_gather) bit for bit, then() output included. The digests are also the same on ring4 and direct.
reason: At T>=6144 candidate-49's project_exchange_rows is faster than the baseline's beyond the interval on both topologies, on max-rank and rank0 medians, and the per-boot 95% CIs do not overlap: ring4 T=6144 c49 [9637.25, 9882.75] vs base [11312.0, 11167.71] us: -13.2% (-1479.9 us) gain; rank0 -14.0% gain; direct T=6144 c49 [8930.53, 8925.02] vs base [10443.04, 11123.68] us: -17.2% (-1855.6 us) gain; rank0 -16.3% gain; at T=8192 -17.9% (ring4) and -18.1% (direct). This is inside the PR's claimed -9.0% to -21.6% at T=6144. Outputs are bit-identical to the baseline's.
notes: Not part of the mark: gather_mxfp8's one-shot route (T<=1024 on ring4, T<=2048 on direct) gains on ring4 at T=160/256 (-33%/-24% max-rank, beyond the interval) but is slower on direct at every routed T (max-rank +9% to +50%, beyond the interval; rank0 beyond at T=512 +18% and T=2048 +25%). The in-process anchor (grouped PyNCCL, same code in both arms) agrees: in the candidate-49 direct runs at T=2048 the anchor's medians are 1,085/1,309 us against 1,610/1,723 us for the routed gather. direct is the sparknet mode the switched shapes serve with, so this route is worth a look at serving level; candidate-49 (without #996) was not worse on any core metric at tp3-switched.

Below the mark's T, project_exchange_rows (slices=1 in both arms) is mostly within the interval; beyond it, ring4 T=160 +18.7% (+250 us, max-rank only), ring4 T=2048 +1.8% and T=4096 +1.5% (+73/+106 us), direct T=4096 rank0 +4.5%; gains at ring4 T=256/512 and direct T=1024/2048 (max-rank). The PR says T=160..4096 do not regress.

Two boots per arm is a narrow interval: at T>=4096 the gather is the same grouped PyNCCL code in both arms, yet direct rank0 shows +11.8%/+13.1% 'beyond the interval' at T=6144/8192 while max-rank is within (-1.5%/+1.1%). Read single small-T 'beyond' cells with that in mind; the T>=6144 project_exchange_rows gains are 1.5-2.8 ms with non-overlapping per-boot CIs.
The PR's README cites max-rank time, its script reports rank 0; both are recorded here.
The PR's two scripts are not in the PR. The copies used as the workload reference were on sp2..sp4 /tmp with mtimes seconds before the PR's receipts on sp1 /tmp; they were read, not run.
Every node was idle, without a hold file, with its GPU lock held, before each run; sp2 was shared with another agent's flock-wrapped jobs, so the first run waited for sp2's lock.

superseded/ holds a first ring4-c49-boot1 whose warm-up may have been under 100 ms of GPU work (its T=6144 result was 9,787 vs anchor 11,963 us), and two launcher attempts that started no container; their numbers are not used.
